newsitem.title: USA: Clinton accepts FCC chairman's resignation.
newsitem.headline: Clinton accepts FCC chairman's resignation.

text.p: President Bill Clinton Tuesday accepted the resignation of Reed Hundt as chairman of the Federal Communications Commission, saying he had been a "strong and visionary leader."
Hundt will leave his post upon appointment of his successor, the White House said.
"Chairman Hundt has been a strong and visionary leader of the FCC during this historic period in telecommunications policy," Clinton said in a statement issued by the White House.
Clinton praised Hundt's "steadfast commitment to the public interest and to bringing the benefits of competition to consumers."
He was appointed chairman by Clinton and took over the job in November 1993. His term was due to expire June 30, 1998.
